# Provider {#sec-provider}

The provider module is found in `backend/core/provider/`. It has two
responsibilities. The family of the backend is recognised, and the noise profile
of a reference machine is chosen. Two files are used: `provider.py` and
`profiles.py`.

## `detect(backend, entangler=None)` {.unnumbered}

The main function of the module. The provider, the entangler and the noise
profile of a backend are returned together in one `BackendInfo` object.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | any object | required | The backend that is injected by Qollab, or a local backend in a test. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` or `None` | `None` | The target entangler. When it is `None`, the entangler is inferred from the name of the backend. |

**Returns** a `BackendInfo` object. See the [Data model](model.qmd) page for its
fields.

**The rules of the entangler.** If the `entangler` parameter is given, it is
used. Otherwise, the name of the backend is checked. A name that contains
`forte` gives `"zz"`. Every other name gives `"ms"`.

**The rule of the hardware.** `is_hardware` is `True` only for an IonQ backend
that is not a simulator. The attribute `_is_simulator` is checked first. If it
does not exist, the word `simulator` in the name is checked.

## `detect_provider(backend)` {.unnumbered}

The family of the backend is found, and one of the five provider names is
returned.

**Parameter**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | any object | The backend to classify. |

**Returns** one of `"ionq"`, `"ibm"`, `"aws"`, `"local"` or `"unknown"`.

**The signals that are used**, in order. A signal is a property of the object,
such as the module of its class or its name.

| Signal | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| the class module starts with `qiskit_ionq`, or the name contains `ionq` | `ionq` |
| the module is `qiskit_ibm_runtime`, the name starts with `fake_` or `ibm_`, or the class is `GenericBackendV2` | `ibm` |
| the module starts with `qiskit_braket_provider`, or the name contains `braket` | `aws` |
| the name or the class contains `BasicSimulator` or `aer_simulator` | `local` |
| anything else | `unknown` |

An unknown provider is never an error. The generic strategy is used instead.

## The noise profiles {.unnumbered}

The file `profiles.py` contains three ready-made profiles.

| Constant | Machine | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARIA` | IonQ Aria | Used for the MS entangler. |
| `FORTE` | IonQ Forte | Used for the ZZ entangler. |
| `IDEAL` | an ideal machine | All fidelities are 1, and all prices are 0. |

The numbers are simple estimates that were taken from public IonQ material. They
are **not** a calibrated noise model. They can be replaced before the demo.

## `get_profile(machine)` {.unnumbered}

A profile is returned by its short name.

**Parameter**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | string | One of `"aria"`, `"forte"` or `"ideal"`. |

**Returns** a `NoiseProfile`.

## `profile_for(provider, name, entangler)` {.unnumbered}

The correct profile is chosen for a backend.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | The provider name. |
| `name` | string | The raw backend name. It is used to find `aria`, `forte` or `ideal`. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The fallback entangler when the name gives no hint. |

**Returns** a `NoiseProfile`.

**The rule.** The name is checked first. A name that contains `ideal` gives the
ideal profile, `forte` gives the Forte profile and `aria` gives the Aria profile.
If the name gives no hint, the reference machine of the entangler is used: Aria
for MS and Forte for ZZ. A non-IonQ backend is therefore shown *as if* it ran on
trapped ions.
